findings.message: The slice `rows[start : start + size + 1]` returns `size + 1` users per page. Each page then also repeats the first user of the next page.
findings.suggestion: return [User(r["id"], r["email"], r["name"]) for r in rows[start : start + size]]

findings.message: Every call now loads the whole `users` table into memory just to return one page. Memory use and latency grow with the table size, which the previous `LIMIT ? OFFSET ?` query avoided. A page number below 1 also gives a negative start, so the slice returns rows from the end of the table.
findings.suggestion:
rows = connection.execute(
        "SELECT id, email, name FROM users ORDER BY id LIMIT ? OFFSET ?", (size, (page - 1) * size)
    ).fetchall()
    return [User(r["id"], r["email"], r["name"]) for r in rows]
